paper.title: When less is more: sketching with minimizers in genomics

evidence.paraphrase: The paper is a broad review of minimizer-based data sketching across genomic applications, including de novo assembly, metagenomics, and pangenomes.
Read alignment is listed only as one application; no iterative alignment, position-wise consensus, or sample-specific reference-refinement loop is described.

reviews.rationale: The abstract supports a general genomics-sketching review rather than sample-specific refinement of a small genome from low-depth reads. Its mention of read alignment gives only a partial analogue to the assigned group and does not establish the group's iterative consensus role.

paper.title: A complete diploid human genome benchmark for personalized genomics

evidence.paraphrase: The study builds a telomere-to-telomere benchmark for the complete diploid human genome and evaluates whole-genome reads, variant calls, and assemblies.
It directly identifies technical and reference biases in reference-mapped human resequencing, providing contextual evidence for the divergent-reference group.
The reported solution is genome-based benchmarking and comparison with de novo assembly, not low-depth refinement of mitochondrial or similarly small genomes.

reviews.rationale: Reference-mapping bias makes this a credible bridge for the divergent-reference group. However, the object and outcome are a complete diploid human-genome benchmark and whole-genome assembly performance, which fall outside the frozen small-genome refinement scope and its exclusion of whole-genome de novo claims.

paper.title: REFCON: Reference-free and robust copy number inference in single-cell tumor transcriptomes

evidence.paraphrase: REFCON infers per-cell copy-number profiles from tumor scRNA-seq rather than refining a mitochondrial, organelle-scale, or similarly small DNA reference.
Its deep-learning model estimates copy-number deviations and optimizes genome-wide profiles; it does not iteratively align short reads to build a consensus reference.

reviews.rationale: The abstract provides enough detail to identify a single-cell tumor transcriptomics copy-number method, not sample-specific small-genome reference refinement. Terms such as reference, profile, and refinement describe a different analytical role, so the iterative-alignment group assignment is a semantic mismatch.
